territorial_scope.description: Applies across the European Union and also reaches non-EU controllers and processors whose processing relates to offering goods or services to, or monitoring, data subjects in the Union.

evidence.quote: This Regulation applies to the processing of personal data of data subjects who are in the Union by a controller or processor not established in the Union

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) sets rules for processing personal data by controllers and processors established in the EU and, under Article 3(2), by non-EU controllers offering goods or services to or monitoring people in the Union. Part 1 covers general provisions, principles, lawful bases, special categories and data subject rights.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) sets rules on protecting natural persons in relation to personal data processing and on its free movement, repealing Directive 95/46/EC. It covers automated processing and filing systems (Art. 2), excluding among others purely household activity and criminal-law enforcement by competent authorities. It binds controllers and processors established in the Union and, for non-EU controllers, those offering goods or services to or monitoring people in the Union (Art. 3). Article 5 sets processing principles with an accountability duty; Article 6 lists six lawful bases; Article 7 sets consent conditions; Article 8 requires parental authorisation for children under 16 using information society services, which Member States may lower to 13. Article 9(1) prohibits processing of special categories of data, subject to listed exceptions. Chapter III grants transparency, information, access, rectification, erasure, restriction and notification rights (Arts. 12-19), with responses due within one month (Art. 12(3)). This annotation covers only the recitals and Articles 1-19 of the text supplied; later chapters and the application date are not described.

notes: Part 1 of 2 covers the title, recitals, and Articles 1 to 19 (Chapters I to III, Sections 1 to 3). Obligations, thresholds, enforcement and most definitions in later Articles, and the operative repeal (Art. 94) and amendment (Art. 95) provisions, are in part 2. Relations are coded from the title and recitals where no operative provision appears in this part. Controllers and processors are roles, not named entities, and no named firms appear in this part. Where no registry ID exists, target_instrument_id is an empty string. Empty lei and ticker are given as empty strings because the schema requires strings. Part 2 covers Articles 20 to 99 (Chapters III to XI) and the footnotes attached to them. Registry IDs for the cited instruments are not assigned, so target_instrument_id is empty. Article 96 (pre-2016 agreements concluded by Member States) and Article 98 (review of other Union data protection acts) name no specific instrument and are not coded as relations. Source typos include 'to a an effective judicial remedy' (Art. 78(2)) and 'monetary, budgetary and taxation a matters' (Art. 23(1)(e)). Article 94(1) (repeal) and Article 99(2) (application from 25 May 2018) both use that date and do not conflict. The section_status entries are set to not_applicable only because the schema requires both keys; the relations and entities sections are populated above.

‘personal data’ means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person
‘processing’ means any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data or on sets of personal data, whether or not by automated means
‘restriction of processing’ means the marking of stored personal data with the aim of limiting their processing in the future
‘profiling’ means any form of automated processing of personal data consisting of the use of personal data to evaluate certain personal aspects relating to a natural person
‘pseudonymisation’ means the processing of personal data in such a manner that the personal data can no longer be attributed to a specific data subject without the use of additional information
‘filing system’ means any structured set of personal data which are accessible according to specific criteria
‘controller’ means the natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data
‘processor’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which processes personal data on behalf of the controller
‘recipient’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or another body, to which the personal data are disclosed, whether a third party or not
‘third party’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or body other than the data subject, controller, processor
‘consent’ of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data subject's wishes
‘personal data breach’ means a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data
‘genetic data’ means personal data relating to the inherited or acquired genetic characteristics of a natural person
‘biometric data’ means personal data resulting from specific technical processing relating to the physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics of a natural person
‘data concerning health’ means personal data related to the physical or mental health of a natural person
as regards a controller with establishments in more than one Member State, the place of its central administration in the Union
‘representative’ means a natural or legal person established in the Union who, designated by the controller or processor in writing pursuant to Article 27
‘enterprise’ means a natural or legal person engaged in an economic activity, irrespective of its legal form
‘group of undertakings’ means a controlling undertaking and its controlled undertakings
‘binding corporate rules’ means personal data protection policies which are adhered to by a controller or processor established on the territory of a Member State
‘supervisory authority’ means an independent public authority which is established by a Member State pursuant to Article 51
a supervisory authority which is concerned by the processing of personal data because
processing of personal data which takes place in the context of the activities of establishments in more than one Member State of a controller or processor in the Union
‘information society service’ means a service as defined in point (b) of Article 1(1) of Directive (EU) 2015/1535
‘international organisation’ means an organisation and its subordinate bodies governed by public international law
one or more independent public authorities to be responsible for monitoring the application of this Regulation
The European Data Protection Board (the ‘Board’) is hereby established as a body of the Union and shall have legal personality.

obligations.summary: Notify the supervisory authority of a personal data breach without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, unless unlikely to result in a risk; include reasons for any delay. Notification content listed in Art. 33(3).

evidence.quote: The controller shall document any personal data breaches, comprising the facts relating to the personal data breach, its effects and the remedial action taken.

obligations.summary: Communicate a personal data breach likely to result in high risk to the data subject without undue delay, in clear and plain language; exemptions in Art. 34(3) (protective measures, subsequent measures, disproportionate effort with public communication).
obligations.conditional_on: Breach likely to result in a high risk to natural persons' rights and freedoms

evidence.quote: the controller shall communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay.

Mandatory cases listed in Art. 35(3).
obligations.conditional_on: Processing likely to result in high risk to natural persons' rights and freedoms

evidence.quote: the controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data.
